Please deliver:
  > 
  > 1. **Main-text Table (the third and last main-text table; label `tab:sparse`)**, width 5.5 in, caption at most 5 lines, one row per subset (eng_full, eng_d30, eng_d50, eng_d70, all_d30, all_d50, name them as in sparse_subsets.csv with a plain-language label such as 'English, 21% observed'). Columns: models x tasks; share of cells observed; median observed cells per tested model; at k=3 with the masked-EM factor model (`fa`): standardised RMSE of the column mean, of random selection, of greedy A, and the relative gap to random with its family-clustered interval (sparse_gap.csv, rel_gap_to_random and the CI of `gap`; say in a note how the relative interval is made if you derive one, otherwise give the absolute gap with CI and the relative point value); closure at k=3 for greedy A and for random with `pw` (sparse_closure.csv); k*(0.9) of greedy A with `pw` with its interval, '>20' for censored (sparse_kstar.csv). Drop columns if the width forces it, in this order: the random RMSE, the column-mean RMSE.
  > 2. **Appendix figure**: standardised RMSE against k (1..20) for column mean, random and greedy A, for `fa` and `pw`, one panel per subset (or three panels with the subsets overlaid, your choice), with the clustered intervals; and an appendix table with the full gap and closure by subset and k=1,3,5,10,20 for both predictors.
  > 3. State in the caption of the table: identity transform only; models with fewer than 30 observed cells not tested; the grid stops at k=20; the LOBO analogue is the better of `fa` and `pw` conditioning on all candidates.
  > 
  > Every number must come from the CSVs. Place: the table goes in Section 6 (experiments) after the dense results; I write the text and will cite it as Table 3. I will shorten other main-text material to fit, so keep the table to about 10 lines in height. Push to `dev` and close this issue.
